widely_grown.gloss: Apples are among the most widely grown fruits.

significance_beyond.gloss: The apple matters beyond nutrition: to agriculture, economics, myth and science.

role_in_civilisation.gloss: The apple has played an important role in human civilisation.

origin_asia.gloss: Domesticated apples come from wild apples in Central Asia, especially Kazakhstan.

sieversii.gloss: Their main wild ancestor, Malus sieversii, still grows there.

spread_trade.gloss: Apples spread west and east with migration and trade.

silk_road_hybrid.gloss: Along the Silk Road, apple populations crossed and gained new traits.

grafting.gloss: Grafting: attaching a branch of a variety onto a rootstock.

seeds_unreliable.gloss: Apple trees grown from seed do not reliably resemble their parents.

grafting_needed.gloss: So growers propagate apples by grafting.

grafting_preserves.gloss: Grafting keeps a variety's flavour, texture and look across generations.

nutrients.gloss: Apples contain fibre, vitamin C and polyphenols.

calories_95.gloss: A medium apple has about 95 calories.

satiety.gloss: Apples' water and fibre make them filling.

apple_a_day.gloss: "An apple a day keeps the doctor away."

no_single_fruit.gloss: No single fruit guarantees health or prevents disease.

meanings_beyond.gloss: Apples have acquired meanings far beyond agriculture.

golden_apples.gloss: Golden apples in Greek myth stand for beauty, desire, immortality or conflict.

eden_apple.gloss: Christian art shows Eden's fruit as an apple, though the Bible names no species.

temptation_symbol.gloss: So the apple became a symbol of temptation and knowledge.

folklore_position.gloss: The apple holds a prominent place in scientific folklore.

newton_story.gloss: Newton reportedly said a falling apple set him thinking about gravity.

ordinary_to_symbol.gloss: An ordinary product can become a powerful cultural symbol.

major_component.gloss: Apple production is a major part of the global fruit industry.

china_largest.gloss: China grows more apples than any other country.

other_producers.gloss: The US, Türkiye, Poland and India also grow apples at scale.

diseases.gloss: Orchards suffer apple scab, fire blight and insect pests.

balance_env.gloss: Growers must balance yields against pesticides, soil and water.

temp_needs.gloss: Apple trees need particular temperatures to flower and fruit.

regions_suitability.gloss: Climate change may make some growing regions less suitable.

breeding_goals.gloss: Breeders want disease resistance, climate resilience, flavour and storage life.

diversity_remarkable.gloss: Genetic diversity is one of the apple's most remarkable features.

thousands_cultivars.gloss: There are thousands of named cultivars, varying in taste, texture and colour.

popular_fraction.gloss: The popular varieties are a small fraction of them.

traits_useful.gloss: Less commercial varieties may carry traits useful for breeding.

preserve_important.gloss: So preserving less commercial varieties matters.

wild_reservoirs.gloss: Wild apples are a valuable source of disease resistance and stress tolerance.

conservation_value.gloss: Conserving apple diversity is a cultural responsibility and a practical investment.

complex_relationship.gloss: The apple illustrates the complex relationship between people and cultivated plants.

history_reflects.gloss: Its history reflects migration, trade, innovation and cultural exchange.

reveals_genetics.gloss: Its biology shows the importance of genetics; its economics the challenges of food production.

useful_perspective.gloss: The apple gives a useful perspective on agriculture and humanity's relation to nature.

deeper_examination.gloss: A deeper look at domestication and genetics would be an interesting extension.
